..
KEY MESSAGE 1... A significant system begins to impact the 
region today with flash flooding and severe weather all on the 
table. The flooding threat will continue into Wednesday. A 
Flood Watch is in place for most of New Jersey, all of eastern 
Pennsylvania, and northern Delaware. 

Update (1130AM). The initial batch of showers and tstms now
across the lower Susqu Valley will push NE across SE PA and up 
into North NJ through the early afternoon. Scattered Severe 
tstms possible as this activity. More isolated showers/tstms for
Delmarva and south/central NJ. After this...more showers will 
form behind the first batch and arrive late afternoon and into 
the evening for all areas. Pops/Wx grids have been adjusted for
these trends. 

Only one key message in the discussion this morning but impacts
are expected to be felt region-wide and over multiple days. The
most significant and impactful day will be today though as a
deepening area of low pressure moves toward New York, with a
warm front lifting through today and a strong cold front coming
in tonight. The front, aided by strong jet dynamics, will
provide ample lift for widespread showers and thunderstorms and
perhaps multiple rounds today and into tonight. 

We will break out the hazards and threats by starting with the
flash flooding threat over the next two days. A lifting warm
front will only strengthen southerly flow through today,
ushering in a very moist airmass. PWATs will approach two 
inches which is over the 90th percentile even for late July. A 
warm cloud layer over 10k feet will also aid in producing very 
efficient rainfall rates. Rates of 1-3" per hour are expected 
later this afternoon and evening. This, combined with the 
potential for multiple rounds of precipitation will result in a 
pretty significant flash flood threat. The WPC Excessive 
Rainfall Outlook reflects that, having a MODERATE (3/4) Risk 
for Excessive Rainfall for Northern New Jersey with a SLIGHT
(2/4) Risk extending through the rest of the region. The biggest
concern will be the more urban areas which begin to see flash 
flooding generally around 1" per hour and that seems very likely
considering today's setup especially in the afternoon and 
evening. Some areas may also be more flood prone, given 
yesterday's rainfall where there were some flooding reports. 

No significant changes in the Flood Watch, which remains in
place for most of New Jersey, all of eastern Pennsylvania, and 
northern Delaware. Lower rainfall amounts and areas more in need
of rainfall over far South Jersey and most of Delmarva will 
result in a lesser flood threat and those areas staying outside 
of the watch. Cannot rule out flash flooding entirely though in 
these areas (as we saw yesterday in localized spots) and most of
South Jersey and Delmarva remains in either a Marginal (1/4) or
Slight (2/4) Risk for Excessive Rainfall. 

The one minor change was extending the Flood Watch north of I-78
through Wednesday. As low pressure meanders, another front will
come through on Wednesday, capable of producing some heavy
downpours yet again for the northern third of the region. This
will move over some more urbanized areas in North Jersey that 
should get a decent amount of rainfall today, potentially 
causing more problems. While mainstem river flooding is not 
currently forecast, some smaller creeks and streams within the 
Passaic and Raritan basins could see some rises that result in 
flooding. 

When all is said and done, the current QPF forecast through
Wednesday has around 2 to 5 inches of rain north of I-78, with 1
to 3 inches elsewhere. As is usual in summer convective setups,
locally higher amounts are possible. HREF Max in northern New
Jersey has highly localized amounts up to 8" through Wednesday.
Have multiple ways to receive any flood alerts. 

In terms of the severe threat, no significant changes were made
to the forecast. Unlike the hydro threat, the severe threat will
be more focused on the southern half of the area. SPC did nudge
the Slight Risk (2/5) a touch south, having far southeast PA,
South Jersey, and all of Delmarva in. The Marginal Risk (1/5) is
in place from Philadelphia on north. Instability will increase
quickly once the warm front passes. Delmarva and South Jersey
will have more time in the warm sector and have higher amounts
of shear to work with. The limiting factor further north towards
Philly and points north will be the amount of cloud cover. Main
timing window is from 2 PM through about 11 PM and damaging 
wind gusts the primary threat. Cannot rule out a tornado, though
the tornado threat will be more focused over Delmarva. No area 
is currently in any severe outlook category for Wednesday. 

Guidance continues to have the surface low to the north potentially
lingering through Thursday, though impacts should mainly be confined
through tomorrow. High pressure nudges in towards the end of the
week and for the weekend, giving us a break from the active pattern.
